items.title: Choosing a p-power exponent that brings a sum of two variables into a prescribed subring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a prime p and positive integers n, m the lemma produces an exponent a such that both the p^a-th power of x+y and p^a(x+y) lie in the subring generated by p^n-th powers and p^n-multiples of x and of y (statement lines 11030-11035). The proof does not invoke a general binomial congruence: it expands the power, decomposes the exponents against p^n and p^m, reduces the claim to the divisibility of a multinomial coefficient by a p-power determined by the remainders, and then estimates the p-adic valuation of those coefficients using the identity expressing a multinomial coefficient as p^a over i times a smaller one (proof lines 11037-11062). The valuation estimate that yields the explicit choice of a is the substance, and the author writes it out. H2.
